faq: What's your typical project timeline?
It depends on scope. A landing page or brand site can land in 1-2 weeks, while a full custom build, e-commerce store or plugin usually runs 3-6 weeks including revisions.
Are you a WordPress developer or a full-stack developer?

Full-stack. I build custom web apps, APIs and features from scratch with JavaScript/React, Node.js, PHP and Python/Django on PostgreSQL. WordPress, Shopify and Webflow are part of my toolkit too, and I reach for them when a platform is the fastest, most practical route for your project.
Can you take over an existing website?
Yes. A lot of the work in this portfolio is maintenance, fixes and new features added to sites I did not originally build.
Do you work with clients remotely?
Yes, every project in this portfolio was delivered remotely, for clients across Nigeria, the UK, Canada and the USA.
What do you need from me to get started?
Access to the hosting/domain (or a plan for getting it), any brand assets you already have, and a short description of what the site needs to do. I can help fill in the gaps from there.
How do I start a project with you?
Fill in my 3-minute project brief. It walks you through your goals, features, timeline and budget, then sends everything to me on WhatsApp or email so I can come back with a clear plan.

cultur-fm-main-project.title: CULTUR FM
cultur-fm-main-project.description: Official CULTUR FM digital platform: homepage, events, mixes and ticketing, powered by three plugins I built from scratch: CULTUR FM Tickets, a multi-event ticketing and gate-validation engine with QR-coded PDF tickets; CFM Waitlist, which runs each event's waitlist, ticket sales, free sign-up and sold-out states; and a Webhook Proxy that sends website form submissions straight into Google Sheets.

highlights.title: CULTUR FM Tickets
highlights.subtitle: Multi-event ticketing & gate validation engine
paragraphs: CULTUR FM's own ticketing system, built from scratch on top of WooCommerce. Each event is set up once in the admin (date, venue, ticket tiers, entry rules, a staff password) and the plugin generates two shortcodes: a ticket-sales widget for the event page and a check-in portal for the door.

Fans pick tickets in a custom sliding bag with live prices, booking fees and per-product currency, enter where to send their tickets, then pay through Stripe, Apple Pay or Paystack. Every order is bound to its event, and a branded PDF ticket with one QR code per guest is generated with Dompdf and emailed automatically.

At the gate, staff log into a password-protected portal that verifies each scan against the event code, order, ticket number and guest name, and refuses duplicates, wrong-event tickets and revoked ones. Admins get a live check-in monitor, a ticket inspector, a security console for chargebacks and fraud, and CSV and PDF exports of guest lists, check-ins and the blacklist.
skills: WooCommerce cart, checkout & order lifecycle hooks
Custom post types, meta boxes & shortcodes
PDF generation (Dompdf) & QR-code ticketing
Ticket validation: anti-duplicate, event binding, revocation
Secure AJAX endpoints with nonces, sessions & role checks
Payments: Stripe, Apple Pay & Paystack flows
CSV / PDF reporting & admin tooling
Mobile-first checkout UX & interactive debugging under production constraints

highlights.title: CFM Waitlist
highlights.subtitle: Custom WordPress Event Management Plugin
paragraphs: Built a bespoke WordPress plugin from scratch for CULTUR FM, a music and culture brand. The plugin manages the full event access lifecycle — waitlist, ticket sales, free signup, and sold-out states — all controlled via a simple admin toggle per event.

Key features include: a custom database table for subscriber management with duplicate detection and email confirmation, GDPR-compliant consent capture, CSV export and bulk email tools for event admins, and a dynamic front-end CTA that automatically renders the correct action based on event state.

On mobile, a fixed sticky bar stays anchored at the bottom of the screen; tapping it opens a modal form with a full dark overlay. The plugin integrates with Advanced Custom Fields and a custom post type, with all logic written in vanilla PHP, JavaScript, and CSS — no page builders, no third-party plugin dependencies.
skills: Custom WordPress plugin development (PHP, no framework)
Vanilla JS (AJAX, DOM manipulation, mobile UX)
CSS architecture (specificity, z-index stacking, mobile-first responsive)
Database design ($wpdb, custom tables, cache-aware queries under Redis / Memcached)
WordPress hooks, AJAX handlers, nonce security
UX problem-solving (multi-state UI, sticky mobile CTA, modal management)
Interactive debugging under production constraints

highlights.title: Webhook Proxy
highlights.subtitle: Elementor forms straight into Google Sheets
paragraphs: A lightweight plugin that connects CULTUR FM's website forms (mix submissions, enquiries and sign-ups) to the team's Google Sheets, so every entry lands in a spreadsheet in real time with no copying and pasting.

It registers a custom WordPress REST endpoint that receives Elementor form webhooks, strips the noise Elementor adds (auto-generated field IDs, IP addresses, browser strings, page URLs, timestamps) and forwards only the real answers to a Google Apps Script.
Each form names its own destination tab, so one endpoint feeds a separate sheet for every form, while links that matter, such as a submitted mix, are kept intact.
skills: WordPress REST API (custom routes & handlers)
Webhooks & server-to-server requests
Google Apps Script & Google Sheets automation
Data cleaning & sanitisation
Elementor Pro forms integration

caseStudy.title: Two full redesigns for one of the biggest DJ platforms in the UK
stats: followers across Instagram, YouTube and TikTok
people served by the ticketing and QR check-in system
waitlist and sign-up registrations, and counting
challenge: I joined CULTUR FM on contract and was handed one of the biggest projects of my career: revamping the main website of a music and culture brand with verified accounts and an audience of over 4 million people across Instagram, YouTube and TikTok.
The site had to carry that scale: events, mixes, merch and, above all, ticket sales that happened on other platforms and pulled fans away from the brand.
approach: I designed a new interface and built it with custom code. A year later the brand evolved, so I designed and developed a second, completely new UI, which is the one live today.

Everything runs inside WordPress and Elementor, extended with plugins and integrations I wrote from scratch, so the team keeps an editor they know while the site does things no theme or off-the-shelf plugin could.
built: Fans buy tickets directly on cultur.fm without leaving the platform: tiered pricing, a custom bag, Stripe, Apple Pay and Paystack checkout.
Branded PDF tickets with a QR code per guest and a staff check-in portal that blocks duplicates, wrong-event and revoked tickets.
My latest product: one plugin that runs each event's waitlist, sign-ups, sales and sold-out states, with 500+ registrations so far.
Website forms flow straight into Google Sheets through a custom REST endpoint and Apps Script.
Two full redesigns in two years, both built on the same custom foundation.
Ticket inspector, security console, live check-in monitor and CSV / PDF exports for the events team.
outcome: A verified, global music platform selling tickets on its own site instead of sending fans elsewhere.
Ticketing and QR check-in that have served over 2 million people over the years.
Still shipping: the waitlist plugin has passed 500 sign-ups and keeps growing.

cultur-totes-project.title: CULTUR FM Totes
cultur-totes-project.description: E-commerce storefront for CULTUR FM's limited-edition Face Totes merchandise, part of the brand's wider digital platform. It runs on WordPress and WooCommerce, but the shopping experience is custom-coded: a branded add-to-bag overlay, a bag icon that only appears once something is in it, and bespoke cart, checkout and thank-you pages.

highlights.title: Custom Shopping Flow
highlights.subtitle: Bespoke bag, cart, checkout & thank-you experience on WooCommerce
paragraphs: Out of the box, WooCommerce looks like every other shop. For CULTUR FM Totes I hand-coded the whole buying journey so it feels like a premium, on-brand store rather than a template.

When a fan taps Add to Bag, a custom overlay in the brand's own typeface confirms the item is being added, then opens the side cart automatically the moment WooCommerce confirms it. The bag icon in the header stays hidden until there is something in it, and stays in sync as items are added or removed, without shifting the navigation.

The cart, checkout and thank-you pages are fully restyled: black-and-white brand styling, dotted-line form fields, a stacked mobile cart layout, 'Cart' renamed to 'Bag' throughout, the default shop pages switched off, and separately tuned layouts for desktop and mobile.
skills: WooCommerce front-end events (added_to_cart, fragments refresh)
Custom JavaScript UI: loading overlay, auto-opening side cart
AJAX endpoint for a live bag count & conditional icon visibility
Custom cart, checkout & thank-you page design (CSS, Elementor, CartFlows)

addoz-project.title: Addoz Integrated Resources Limited
addoz-project.description: ADDOZ is a recruitment platform for Addoz Integrated Resources, a Lagos HR outsourcing and recruitment consultancy. I rebuilt it from a limited WordPress site into a custom Next.js application with candidate, employer and admin workspaces, an approval-based job marketplace and secure CV handling.

caseStudy.title: From a stuck WordPress site to a custom recruitment platform
challenge: Addoz's first website was built on WordPress. A real recruitment marketplace needs things WordPress was never designed for: separate candidate, employer and admin accounts, a job approval workflow, secure CV handling, messaging and notifications.

Every feature meant another plugin or workaround, key functionality couldn't be reached, the site wasn't working reliably and there was no room to grow. I was called in to revamp it into something properly custom.
approach: After weighing headless WordPress and off-the-shelf recruitment software (which would have meant plugin hacks, per-seat pricing and someone else's branding), I rebuilt ADDOZ from scratch as a modular Next.js application the client fully owns.

Job pages are server-rendered for search engines, every database query is typed, every form input is validated on the server, and each workspace is protected by role-based access checked before a page even renders.
built: Search and filter by keyword, category, location, job type, workplace, experience and salary, with company, category and Lagos / Ogun location pages and a sitemap generated from live jobs.
Applications and their status, saved jobs, job alerts, profile, CV and direct messages with employers.
Post roles (draft → in review → live), review applicants with CV download and hiring stages, plus analytics and a company profile.
Approve or decline every job with a reason, preview any job privately, suspend or remove accounts, moderate messages and broadcast notifications, with every action written to an audit log.
Signed-in candidates apply in a few taps; guests apply with a CV and quietly get a passwordless account so all their applications stay together.
Email and password sign-in with 6-digit email verification and password reset; roles (candidate, employer, admin) are owned by the server, never the browser.
Resume scanner, interview prep and cover-letter tools that work instantly in the browser.
In-app and email alerts for applications, stage changes, job approvals and new messages.
outcome: Live at addozconsultinglimited.com, replacing the old WordPress site.
No plugin ceilings or per-seat software fees: the client owns every feature, page and line of code.
Three role-based workspaces and an admin approval workflow, built to grow with the business.

highlights.subtitle: Kitchen prep automation for WooCommerce restaurants
highlights.badge: My own product · Free plan available
paragraphs: PrepMaster is a product I designed and built from scratch for restaurants that take orders through WooCommerce. It turns the day's orders into ready-to-use kitchen prep sheets automatically, so the kitchen knows exactly what to prepare without tallying tickets by hand.

A WordPress plugin written in PHP hooks into WooCommerce order data and works with a Node.js backend and PostgreSQL database. Restaurants, packages and product mapping are managed from a dedicated admin area with its own dashboard, prep-sheet views, a health check and built-in debug tools.

Licensing, subscriptions and pricing run on the Freemius SDK, from license-key activation to plan upgrades: a Free plan to get started (1 restaurant, 20 orders a month, basic prep sheets), Pro at $89.99/year for growing restaurants with unlimited orders and auto product mapping, and Business at $249.99/year for up to 10 restaurants with analytics, report exports, email notifications and multi-user access.
skills: WordPress plugin architecture (PHP, WooCommerce hooks & order data)
Node.js backend & PostgreSQL database design
SaaS licensing & subscriptions with the Freemius SDK
Tiered pricing, plan limits & feature gating
Admin UX: dashboards, prep-sheet views, product mapping
Health checks, debug tooling & recovery-mode testing
Product thinking: from a kitchen problem to a paid product

caseStudy.title: From one client's problem to a product with paying users
stats: countries: Nigeria, UK, USA and Ghana
challenge: A client hired me to build a restaurant and small-chops delivery website. After launch, she told me about a problem that had been eating into the business for a long time, and said she'd be happy if anyone could take it off her plate.
She described it, and that problem became PrepMaster: turning each day's orders into kitchen prep sheets automatically.
approach: I built it for her as a separate application. Then I thought: if one restaurant needs this, many do. So I turned it into my own product, a WordPress plugin with a Node.js and PostgreSQL backend, sold with Free, Pro and Business plans through Freemius.
outcome: Over 100 users and around 20 paying customers across Nigeria, the UK, the USA and Ghana.
A real SaaS product that grew out of listening to one client.

snap-and-stem-main-project.title: Snap & Stem Creative Studio
snap-and-stem-main-project.description: Main website for Snap & Stem Creative Studio, where flowers meet artistry: a shop for bouquets and vase arrangements alongside the studio's story and mission, built to sit beside its photography site. Includes custom-built Shopify-style tipping at checkout and an IP-aware English / Canadian French language switcher.

highlights.title: Add a Tip
highlights.subtitle: Shopify-style tipping for a WooCommerce checkout
paragraphs: Built a custom tipping feature for Snap & Stem's WooCommerce store, so customers can thank the florists and photographers at checkout the same way Shopify stores let them: one tap on a preset percentage, or a custom amount of their choice.

The tip is calculated from the live cart subtotal and added to the order as a proper WooCommerce cart fee, so it appears in the order totals, the order record and the confirmation emails, and works through the store's FunnelKit checkout with Moneris, Apple Pay and Google Pay.
Totals update instantly over AJAX with no page reload, and the controls are designed mobile-first to sit naturally in the shop's checkout.
skills: WooCommerce cart fees API & checkout hooks
PHP hooks & filters, AJAX endpoints with nonce security
FunnelKit checkout customisation
Payment-flow compatibility (Moneris, Apple Pay, Google Pay)
JavaScript for live order-total updates
Mobile-first checkout UX

highlights.title: EN ⇄ FR Switcher
highlights.subtitle: IP-aware English / Canadian French language switcher
paragraphs: A custom WordPress plugin for Snap & Stem, a studio in Casselman, Ontario, that serves both English and French-speaking Canadians. First-time visitors get a bilingual welcome and choose English or Canadian French with a tactile 3D toggle, and the plugin then hands off to Weglot to serve the translated site.

It looks up the visitor's location by IP, so people in French-speaking regions such as Québec and New Brunswick are offered French first. Their choice is saved through a nonce-protected AJAX request to a 30-day cookie, so the selector never appears twice.

A settings page in the WordPress admin lets the team set Weglot's French URL path and limit the selector to the homepage. The modal is accessible (an ARIA dialog), uses inline SVG flags and is built with PHP, jQuery and CSS, with no page builder.
skills: WordPress plugin development (PHP, hooks, admin settings page)
IP geolocation & region-based language defaults
Weglot integration & multilingual URL routing
AJAX with nonce verification, cookie-based persistence
Accessible modal UI (ARIA dialog) & 3D CSS toggle
Bilingual UX for English and Canadian French audiences

caseStudy.title: A detail-obsessed client, a sleek shop and a retainer
challenge: I was referred by my brother, a very professional and talented brand identity designer, to design a floral website. The client's attention to detail is top-notch, so after weeks of back and forth we agreed the brief: something sleek, not over-decorated, that performs well.
approach: Then Snap & Stem came alive: a clean WooCommerce shop for bouquets and arrangements, with custom-built Shopify-style tipping at checkout and an IP-aware English / Canadian French language switcher.
outcome: The client was so happy that I was kept on a retainer.
The website has made over CA$16,000 in sales.
He then gave me the Photography side of the business because of how the first site went.
